stories.headline: Senate Impeachment Court Eyes Whole-Day October Sessions Before Budget Work
stories.deck: The tentative calendar would expand hearing hours on selected October dates, pause during intensive budget work and resume in November.
body: The Senate impeachment court is considering whole-day trial sessions beginning at 10 a.m. on selected October dates to allow more witnesses to be heard before the chamber's intensive work on the 2027 national budget.

Presiding Officer Francis Escudero outlined possible whole-day sessions on Oct. 1 and 2, Oct. 5 to 9, and Oct. 12 to 15. No hearings would be held from Oct. 16 to Nov. 8 under the tentative plan, with limited sessions resuming in November.
Escudero said the calendar remained tentative and would be finalized after senators agree on how to balance the impeachment trial with budget responsibilities.
Longer hearing days could allow two or three witnesses to be heard in a day and reduce the overall number of trial dates without displacing the Senate's budget timetable.

stories.headline: Visayas and Mindanao Grids Placed Under Extended Red Alerts
stories.deck: The Visayas grid faced a nine-hour red alert while Mindanao was also under red alert for much of the day as available capacity remained tight.
body: NGCP placed both the Visayas and Mindanao grids under red alert on September 3 because available capacity and operating reserves were insufficient for demand and contingency requirements.
Consumers and businesses should monitor NGCP and local distribution-utility advisories for changes in alert periods and supply restoration.
The Visayas red alert was scheduled from 1 p.m. to 10 p.m., while Mindanao was under red alert from noon to 9 p.m.

Available capacity in the Visayas was about 2,187 MW against projected peak demand of 2,575 MW. NGCP cited forced outages, long-term unavailable units and derated plants, with total capacity losses reported at about 792 MW.

stories.headline: DepEd Estimates ₱7.783 Billion Needed to Repair Schools Hit by Habagat and Cyclones
stories.deck: The estimate covers immediate cleanup, minor and major repairs, and reconstruction of heavily damaged school sites.
body: The Department of Education estimated that rehabilitation of schools damaged by floods, the southwest monsoon and recent tropical cyclones would require about ₱7.783 billion.
The final pace of repairs will depend on funding releases, damage validation, procurement and the ability to keep learning going while facilities are restored.
More than 11,000 classrooms were affected nationwide.

DepEd's estimate included about ₱65.036 million for cleanup and clearing at 2,243 schools, ₱319.97 million for minor repairs at 1,487 schools, ₱1.194 billion for major repairs at 669 schools and about ₱5.62 billion to reconstruct 490 heavily damaged school sites.

stories.headline: Ombudsman Dismisses Former BFP Chief, Files Bribery and Graft Charges Over ₱485M Ambulance Deal
stories.deck: The anti-graft office said its investigation found grounds to administratively dismiss Jesus Fernandez and bring criminal charges tied to the procurement of 132 ambulances. The criminal allegations remain for the courts to determine.
body: The Office of the Ombudsman has dismissed former Bureau of Fire Protection chief Jesus Fernandez from government service and filed criminal charges against him before the Sandiganbayan over an ambulance procurement worth about ₱485 million.
The case grew out of a complaint filed by the Department of the Interior and Local Government after a fact-finding investigation into the procurement of 132 Type 1 Basic Life Support ambulances.
The case concerns procurement for emergency medical vehicles funded through government spending, making the integrity of the bidding and purchasing process a direct public-interest issue.

The next material developments include the Sandiganbayan’s handling of the criminal cases, any plea or defense filed by Fernandez and Sangga, and whether either party challenges the Ombudsman’s administrative ruling through available legal remedies.

stories.headline: Two Filipino Seafarers Killed in Strait of Hormuz Tanker Attack
stories.deck: The deaths renewed calls for strict enforcement of Filipino seafarers' right to refuse voyages through designated high-risk areas.
body: The Department of Migrant Workers confirmed that two Filipino seafarers were killed after the Saudi-flagged crude oil tanker SIDR was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
Families and surviving crew members will be watching the delivery of compensation, insurance, repatriation support and enforcement of high-risk-area protections.

The Philippine government said the victims were from Cabuyao, Laguna, and Daanbantayan, Cebu, and ordered agencies to provide their families with applicable benefits, compensation and insurance assistance.

Senator Raffy Tulfo called on the DMW to ensure that manning agencies and shipping companies respect Filipino seafarers' right to refuse sailing through designated high-risk areas without losing benefits.

stories.headline: Free Toll Implemented Between Pulilan and San Fernando; RFID Users to Get Refunds
stories.deck: The waiver was introduced as flooding near Tulaoc Bridge in San Simon caused severe traffic disruption along the expressway.
body: The Department of Transportation secured a toll waiver for all vehicle classes traveling between Pulilan, Bulacan, and San Fernando, Pampanga, and vice versa, as flooding near the Tulaoc Bridge disrupted NLEX traffic.
Motorists should monitor NLEX and TRB advisories for the duration of the waiver, account adjustments and changes in road conditions around San Simon.

The Toll Regulatory Board said motorists using RFID could initially see normal charges posted to their accounts, but the toll operator would perform backroom adjustments to return charges covered by the waiver.
The toll relief reduced the financial burden on motorists already facing unusually long delays caused by flood-related traffic conditions.
